questions.question: Two identical positive charges \(Q\) each are fixed at a distance of ' \(2 a\) ' apart from each other. questions.explanation:
Resultant force on charge \(q_0\)
\[
F_R=\left\{\frac{k Q q_0}{(a-x)^2}-\frac{k Q q_0}{(a+x)^2}\right\}
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
& =-k Q q_0\left\{\frac{a^2+x^2+2 a x-a^2-x^2+2 a x}{\left(a^2-x^2\right)^2}\right\} \\
& F_R=-\frac{k Q q_0(4 a x)}{\left(a^2-x^2\right)^2}

\]

From Newtons second law, \(a=\frac{F}{m}\)

questions.question: A pulley of radius \(1.5 m\) is rotated about its axis by a force \(F=\left(12 t-3 t^2\right) N\) applied tangentially (while \(t\) is measured in seconds). questions.explanation:
[18] \(r=1.5 m , F=12 t-3 t^2 N , I=4.5 kgm ^2\)
Torque, \(\tau=I \alpha\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \alpha=\frac{\tau}{I}=\frac{1.5 \times\left(12 t-3 t^2\right)}{4 \cdot 5}=\frac{1}{3}\left(12 t-3 t^2\right) \\
& \Rightarrow \alpha=4 t-t^2 \\
& \frac{d \omega}{d t}=4 t-t^2=\int d \omega=\int\left(4 t-t^2\right)_0^t d t \\
& \omega=2 t^2-\frac{t^3}{3}
\end{aligned}
\]

For \(\omega=0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
& 0=2 t^2-\frac{t^3}{3}=t^2\left(2-\frac{t}{3}\right)=0 \\
& t=0,6 s
\end{aligned}
\]

Since, \(\omega=\frac{d \theta}{d t} \Rightarrow d \theta=\omega d t\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \int_0^0 d \theta=\int_0^6\left(2 t^2-\frac{t^3}{3}\right) d t \\
& \theta=\left[\frac{2 t^3}{3}-\frac{t^4}{12}\right]=\left[\frac{t^2}{3}\left(2 t-\frac{t^2}{4}\right)\right]_0^6 \\
& =\frac{36}{3}\left(12-\frac{36}{4}\right)=36 rad
\end{aligned}
\]

No. of revolutions \(=\frac{36}{2 \pi}=\frac{18}{\pi} \Rightarrow k=18\)

questions.explanation:
Let \(F(x,y)=y^5-9xy+2x\).

Implicit differentiation gives

\(5y^4\dfrac{dy}{dx}-9\left(y+x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)+2=0\).

Therefore, \((5y^4-9x)\dfrac{dy}{dx}=9y-2\).

Hence, \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{9y-2}{5y^4-9x}\).

For a tangent parallel to the \(x\)-axis,

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\).

Therefore, \(9y-2=0\), so \(y=\dfrac29\).

Substituting in the curve,

\(y^5+x(2-9y)=y^5=0\),

which is impossible for \(y=\dfrac29\).

Hence, \(M=0\).

For a tangent parallel to the \(y\)-axis,

\(5y^4-9x=0\).

Therefore, \(x=\dfrac{5y^4}{9}\).

Substituting in the curve,

\(y^5-5y^5+\dfrac{10y^4}{9}=0\).

Thus, \(y^4\left(\dfrac{10}{9}-4y\right)=0\).

Hence, \(y=0\) or \(y=\dfrac5{18}\).

For \(y=0\), \(x=0\),

and the numerator \(9y-2=-2\) is non-zero.

For \(y=\dfrac5{18}\), \(x=\dfrac59\left(\dfrac5{18}\right)^4\),

and the numerator \(9y-2=\dfrac12\) is non-zero.

Therefore, both points have vertical tangents.

Hence, \(N=2\).

Thus, \(M+N=0+2=2\).

The mean and variance of 10 observation were calculated as 15 and 15 respectively by a student who took by mistake 25 instead of 15 for one observation. Then, the correct standard deviation is

questions.explanation:
For the wrongly calculated data, \(\sum x_i=10\times 15=150\).

Using \(\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum x_i^2}{n}-\bar{x}^{\,2}\), we get \(\sum x_i^2=10(15+15^2)=2400\).

The observation \(15\) was recorded as \(25\).

\(\Rightarrow \text{Correct sum}=150-25+15=140\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{Correct mean}=\dfrac{140}{10}=14\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{Correct sum of squares}=2400-25^2+15^2=2000\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{Correct variance}=\dfrac{2000}{10}-14^2=200-196=4\)

\(\Rightarrow \text{Correct standard deviation}=\sqrt{4}=2\)

The required value is \(2\).
